teams.heading: Maro Itoje explains his decision to sit out summer Test matches
teams.body: England captain Maro Itoje has defended his decision to take a mini-sabbatical during the recent Nations Championship, describing the move as a "wise and prudent decision." After a gruelling year, the 31-year-old missed the summer series against South Africa, Fiji, and Argentina to prioritise mental and physical recovery. While admitting it felt "very weird" watching from afar, Itoje believes that such proactive breaks are essential for leading players to prolong their careers ahead of the 2027 World Cup.

teams.heading: World Rugby bans Gonzalo Quesada following critical match official abuse comments
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada has become the first head coach sanctioned under the new Match Official Abuse Sanctioning Process introduced by World Rugby in July. The governing body issued a two-test suspension after determining that the Italy coach made unacceptable comments regarding the performance of referee Luc Ramos during the July meeting with New Zealand. The new disciplinary framework was agreed upon during the Shape of the Game forum to address increasing concerns regarding public criticism directed at match officials.

teams.heading: High Court allows concussion claims against rugby governing bodies to continue
teams.body: The ongoing legal challenge involving hundreds of former players seeking damages for neurological injuries remains unresolved. The High Court has recently permitted the class action lawsuits to proceed, rejecting attempts by World Rugby and other governing bodies to have the claims thrown out. The litigation, which focuses on alleged failures to protect players from the long-term risks of concussion, is expected to continue as the parties prepare for trial. No final judgment or settlement has yet been reached.
